careers.title: Software Developer
careers.summary: Designs, builds, tests and maintains software applications and services.
careers.education: Computer science, software engineering, information technology or equivalent practical training.

salary.note: Use current Ethiopian job advertisements for live local ranges.

ethiopia.trend: Ethiopia's digital ecosystem is expanding, increasing opportunities for software and digital-service skills.

international.trend: Software demand is supported by AI, IoT, automation, security and connected products.

commonQuestions.question: Can I become a developer without a computer science degree?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes. A degree can help, but practical skills, projects, problem solving and evidence of ability can also matter.

commonQuestions.question: What should I learn first?
commonQuestions.answer: Start with programming fundamentals, Git and the core technologies used in your target development area.

commonQuestions.question: How can I get experience?
commonQuestions.answer: Build projects, contribute to open source, complete internships and create a portfolio.

professionalStoryQuestions: How did you get your first developer job?
Which skills helped you most?
What would you learn differently if you started again?

careers.title: Cybersecurity Analyst
careers.summary: Protects systems, networks, applications and data from security threats.
careers.education: Cybersecurity, computer science, IT or related training; certifications can help.

salary.note: Verify current Ethiopian vacancies before displaying a numerical local range.

ethiopia.trend: Growing digital services and connectivity increase the need for security capabilities across finance, telecom, government and technology.

international.trend: Cybersecurity demand is driven by increasing cyber threats and expanding digital systems.

commonQuestions.question: Do I need programming for cybersecurity?
commonQuestions.answer: Not every role requires advanced programming, but scripting becomes increasingly useful as you progress.

commonQuestions.question: Should I learn networking first?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes. Networking fundamentals make many security concepts easier to understand.

commonQuestions.question: What is a SOC analyst?
commonQuestions.answer: A SOC analyst monitors security events, investigates suspicious activity and helps respond to incidents.

professionalStoryQuestions: How did you enter cybersecurity?
Which lab helped you get started?
Which skill made the biggest difference?

careers.title: Data Analyst
careers.summary: Turns data into useful information for business and operational decisions.
careers.education: Data analytics, statistics, mathematics, computer science, business or equivalent practical training.

salary.note: Verify current Ethiopian vacancies for numerical ranges.

ethiopia.trend: Digitization increases the value of reporting, dashboards and data-driven decision support.

international.trend: Growth is supported by increasing data volumes and data-driven decision making.

commonQuestions.question: Do I need advanced mathematics?
commonQuestions.answer: You need useful statistics and analytical reasoning, but not necessarily advanced mathematics for entry-level analyst roles.

commonQuestions.question: Excel or SQL first?
commonQuestions.answer: Excel is a friendly starting point; SQL becomes essential when working with relational databases.

commonQuestions.question: What should be in my portfolio?
commonQuestions.answer: Include cleaned datasets, SQL analysis, dashboards and explanations of the decisions your analysis supports.

professionalStoryQuestions: How did you get your first analytics role?
Which portfolio project helped you most?
What business skill surprised you by being important?

careers.title: IT Support Specialist
careers.summary: Helps users solve hardware, software, account, network and technical problems.
careers.education: IT, computer science, networking or practical technical training.

salary.note: Use current local job advertisements for salary figures.

ethiopia.trend: IT support remains relevant wherever organizations operate computers, networks, cloud services and business applications.

international.trend: Automation reduces some support tasks, while replacement openings continue to create opportunities.

commonQuestions.question: Is IT support a good first tech job?
commonQuestions.answer: It can provide practical experience with users, systems, networks, security and troubleshooting.

commonQuestions.question: Do I need a degree?
commonQuestions.answer: Requirements vary; some roles accept certifications, practical experience or relevant coursework.

commonQuestions.question: Can IT support lead to cybersecurity?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes. Networking, operating systems, identity management and troubleshooting provide useful foundations.

professionalStoryQuestions: How did you get your first IT support role?
What troubleshooting skill did you learn first?
How did you move into another IT role?

careers.title: Network Administrator
careers.summary: Installs, configures, monitors and maintains organizational networks.
careers.education: Networking, IT, computer science or related technical training.

salary.note: Verify current local vacancies for numerical salary ranges.

ethiopia.trend: Connectivity expansion and digital infrastructure create continuing requirements for network skills.

international.trend: Traditional administrator employment is projected to decline while cloud and network architecture skills remain relevant.

commonQuestions.question: Is networking still useful with cloud?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes. Cloud environments still depend on IP addressing, routing, DNS, security and connectivity.

commonQuestions.question: Should I learn Cisco?
commonQuestions.answer: Cisco is useful for learning networking and for roles that use Cisco equipment, but concepts transfer to other vendors.

commonQuestions.question: Can networking lead to cybersecurity?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes. Strong networking knowledge is useful for many security roles.

professionalStoryQuestions: What networking concept took you longest to understand?
Which lab helped you learn?
How did you get your first infrastructure role?

careers.title: UI/UX Designer
careers.summary: Designs digital interfaces and experiences based on user needs, research and usability principles.
careers.education: Design, HCI, visual communication or practical portfolio-based training.

salary.note: Verify current local vacancies for numerical salary ranges.

ethiopia.trend: Expansion of digital products and services increases demand for usable interfaces and customer-focused design.

salary.note: UX/product-design titles vary widely, so use current role-specific sources.

growthProjection.note: Use current digital-design and product-design data rather than one universal UX forecast.

international.trend: Digital products, accessibility, research and design systems remain common requirements.

commonQuestions.question: Do I need coding?
commonQuestions.answer: Not always. Basic HTML, CSS and frontend concepts can improve collaboration with developers.

commonQuestions.question: Is Figma enough for a portfolio?
commonQuestions.answer: Figma is a tool; a strong portfolio explains the problem, research, decisions, iterations and outcome.

commonQuestions.question: UI vs UX?
commonQuestions.answer: UI focuses heavily on interface and visual interaction; UX covers the broader experience, user needs, research and usability.

professionalStoryQuestions: How did you build your first design portfolio?
How do you conduct user research?
How do you work with developers?

salary.note: Verify current Ethiopian vacancies before displaying numerical estimates.

salary.note: Use current BLS accountant/auditor data for numerical figures.

commonQuestions.question: Is accounting only calculations?
commonQuestions.answer: No. Accounting also involves reporting, controls, analysis, communication, compliance and business operations.

commonQuestions.question: Is Excel important?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes. Spreadsheet skills are widely useful for accounting analysis and reporting.

careers.title: Digital Marketing Specialist
careers.summary: Uses digital channels, content, analytics and campaigns to reach audiences and support business goals.
careers.education: Marketing, communications, business or practical digital-marketing training.

salary.note: Verify current Ethiopian vacancies for numerical salary data.

ethiopia.trend: Growth in online services, e-commerce, digital products and social-media use creates opportunities for digital marketing skills.

salary.note: Salary varies heavily by specialization and market; use current job postings.

growthProjection.note: Track specialist occupations such as market research, advertising and marketing management.

commonQuestions.question: Can I start without a degree?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes. Portfolio projects, campaign experiments, analytics knowledge and communication can demonstrate practical ability.

commonQuestions.question: Which skill should I learn first?
commonQuestions.answer: Start with marketing fundamentals, content, analytics and one channel such as SEO or social media.

careers.title: Project Manager
careers.summary: Plans and coordinates projects, resources, schedules, risks, stakeholders and delivery.
careers.education: Business, project management, technology, engineering or related field; practical experience is important.

ethiopia.marketStatus: Used across technology, construction, consulting, NGOs, finance, telecom and development organizations

salary.note: Verify current role-specific vacancies because compensation differs strongly by sector and seniority.

ethiopia.trend: Project coordination skills are transferable across many growing sectors, including digital services and infrastructure.
ethiopia.source: World Bank jobs and digital-sector reporting

salary.note: Project manager titles cover many occupations; use role-specific salary sources.

growthProjection.note: Track project-management-specialist and industry-specific management occupations separately.

international.trend: Agile delivery, cross-functional coordination, risk management and digital project tools are common requirements.

commonQuestions.question: Do project managers need to be technical?
commonQuestions.answer: Not always, but technical understanding is valuable when managing technology projects.

commonQuestions.question: Can I become a project manager without starting as one?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes. Many people begin as coordinators or specialists and gradually take responsibility for planning and delivery.
